title: SSE graceful drain and late-chunk integration for hosted streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-severity customer escalations reported missing tokens and duplicated or orphaned partial chunks when a client disconnects and reconnects during Hosted API SSE streams. Incident clarified two modes of failure: (1) server-initiated truncate when downstream queue is drained during failover, resulting in lost suffix tokens; (2) late-arriving chunks from in-flight GPU workers that are not merged because the reassembly window was closed on disconnect. This ticket implements a graceful drain + late-chunk integration strategy on the server side to preserve forward progress, reduce duplication, and avoid delivering incoherent partial outputs to clients.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a long-generation request via hosted /v1/streams endpoint with token rate that triggers batching and KV cache hits
Simulate intermittent network disconnect from client at random offsets mid-stream (client closes connection without sending an explicit EOF)
Trigger node failover by draining the serving instance (scale-down or simulated GC pause) while the request is in-flight
Reconnect the client and attempt resume via existing resume-token/sequence-number handshake
Observe missing suffix tokens, duplicate tokens, or dangling partial messages in the resumed stream in production traffic replay
related_customer_reports: support-ticket-#18392 (large fintech customer) - truncated summaries observed in production after reconnect
escalation-email-2025-11-09 from partner-integrations - duplicate sentence fragments after reconnect
proposed_fix: Introduce a two-part server protocol: (A) graceful drain marker that keeps a short reassembly window open for a configurable tail period (default 2s) after detecting a client disconnect or container drain; and (B) idempotent late-chunk merge where late fragments tagged with the original request id and sequence numbers are reconciled into the active reassembly buffer if they arrive within the tail window. Add precise duplicate suppression using chunk fingerprinting and strict sequence checks. Ensure that resume handshake validates token continuity and falls back to explicit replay if gaps are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Resume handshake rejects only when a true sequence gap exists (>=1 missing token) and returns a machine-readable gap report
Late chunks arriving within the drain tail window (default 2s) are merged into the resumed stream without producing duplicates or reordering
If late chunks arrive after the tail window, server logs an attachable artifact showing why fragments were dropped and surfaces a deterministic fallback to partial re-generation
End-to-end integration tests that simulate disconnect + node drain pass in CI with deterministic assertions on token continuity
Latency regression <2% on synthetic streaming benchmarks when running with tail window enabled
Customer reports from the two escalations show resolution: no truncated outputs observed in a 48h post-deploy monitoring window
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Triage call with on-call, infra, and runtime teams. Confirmed reproduction in customer traffic replay (run 2025-11-11-replay-06).
2025-11-14: Design meeting - choose tail window approach + sequence-aware idempotency. Agreed default tail_window_ms=2000 and fingerprinting via sha1(seq_range|request_id).
2025-11-16: Spike implemented in runtime branch feat/sse-drain-tail - prototype keeps reassembly buffer open for configured tail window after disconnect. End-to-end unit tests added.

2025-11-18: Integration tests flapping on heavy batch configurations due to race in worker completion callback. Mitigation added: worker callback now sequentializes merge through single reassembly actor. Running additional CI runs.
2025-11-19: Code review open - PR #5546. Need security review for log payloads that may include user prompt snippets before shipping.

dashboards_and_alerts: SLOs impacted: hosted-stream-availability (current burn observed during incident)
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy to canary subset of hosted traffic (5%) with tail_window_ms=2000 and duplication suppression enabled
2) Monitor gap_rate and dup_chunk_rate and run automated integration tests against canary instances
3) If metrics are stable for 24h, expand to 25% and run 12h regression checks
4) Full rollout (100%) if no regressions and latency target within 2%
5) If regression detected, automatic rollback to previous runtime image and notify on-call
qa_plan: Add deterministic CI scenarios that simulate: reconnect within tail window, reconnect after tail window, worker late-emit with overlapping seq ranges
Load test synthetic traffic with diversified batch sizes to validate no latency cliffs
Manual verification with customer replay of the two escalations - run acceptance harness and record diff of resumed outputs
Security review of logs and telemetry to ensure no PHI or secrets are persisted in new diagnostic artifacts
notes: Implementation must be compatible with Dedicated and Private runtimes; gating via config flags at serve-time (enable_drain_tail=true) is required to avoid surprising enterprise customers.
Consider later iteration: expose resume diagnostics via console for customer support to triage reconstructions without asking for full request payloads.
Follow-up: add end-to-end encrypted attachable artifact upload for fragments dropped after tail window so we can share redacted evidence with customers during postmortem.
